title: Adaptive risk-weighted tranche prioritization for quarterly private/on-prem rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a repeatable, evidence-driven method to convert a large backlog of private/VPC/on-prem upgrade tasks into quarterly rollout tranches that balance customer risk, revenue impact, upgrade complexity, and capacity constraints. Current approaches are ad-hoc (manual spreadsheets and tribal knowledge) and produce brittle waves that either over-index on low-risk tenants or leave high-revenue customers waiting.

Goal: Deliver an 'adaptive risk-weighted tranche prioritization' framework and lightweight tooling for Q2 2025 that: 1) scores tenants and features on a standardized risk/reward vector, 2) produces tranche recommendations respecting SLOs/failure budgets and engineering capacity, and 3) surfaces tranche-level OKRs and acceptance criteria in the PM Console.

Scope: Private/VPC/on-prem customers for release windows in Q2 2025. Workstreams: scoring methodology, tranche generator (spreadsheet + small utility), rollout constraints encoder (failure budgets, region capacity), Console dashboard prototype for PMs & Sales, and playbook for customer communications and rollback gates.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring model defined and documented: formula and weights for compatibility surface, upgrade complexity, SLA sensitivity, revenue, and past incident rate (Confluence doc linked).
Tranche generator provides top-3 tranche proposals for a given release window and capacity profile; proposals exported as CSV for ops and as JSON for automation.
Console prototype exposes tranche composition, OKR mappings, and per-tranche failure budget; PM and SE stakeholders can preview and comment.
Cross-functional sign-off obtained from Eng Reliability, Sales Ops, and Legal for the recommended rollout gating rules.
Runbook with communication templates and rollback criteria published in Confluence and linked to the release playbook.
